After closing, working rules for travel paperwork
New handlers should know what to do first

This page covers after-closing work for the Companion Animal Travel Desk of Aurelia Skyways, because clean paperwork keeps live-animal travel moving without delay. Your first task is to check every case file for missing forms, mixed-up pet details, or stray notes left by the day shift. Safety takes priority over speed in every journey, so slow, careful review is the correct pace when the counter is quiet.

Start with the travel packet, then match the booking record to the health papers, crate notes, and service remarks. If a form looks unclear, pause and bring it to the senior coordinator before you stamp or file anything. <<FACT F073>> Keep the rest of the file aligned so the next handler can see the status at a glance.

For rabbits, make sure the health certificate is current and filed with the rest of the journey papers. <<FACT F082>> Do not guess when a document looks close enough; if there is doubt, route it upward and wait for a clear decision. This protects the traveler and keeps the service record clean.

For birds, check the combined pet and crate limit before you approve the file. <<FACT F065>> If the weight note is missing, unreadable, or attached to the wrong traveler, stop the process and ask for a corrected version. Never rely on memory when the crate label and booking copy do not match.

When the desk is clear, stack completed files by route, then place holds and unresolved cases in the exception tray. Mark any action taken in plain language, using short notes that another handler can follow fast. Riley may appear in the pet notes, and that is fine as long as the file stays complete and legible.

Remember to close each shift by checking accuracy first, then filing cleanly, and then handing over only what is ready for the next day.
